skills.title: Account has passed its end date
skills.description: Use when most failures carry the account-expired code. The account itself has reached its configured end date, which is different from an expired password, and needs an extension request or retirement.

skills.title: Sign-in blocked by access policy
skills.description: Use when most Entra ID sign-in failures carry a Conditional Access block code. The sign-in was stopped by access policy, such as device, location, client app or risk requirements, and not by a wrong password.

skills.title: Something is still using a disabled account
skills.description: Use when most failures carry the account-disabled code in Active Directory or Entra ID. The password is not the problem: the account is disabled and a system or person is still trying to use it.

skills.title: Sign-ins stopped at the MFA step
skills.description: Use when most Entra ID sign-in entries are multi-factor or additional-verification interrupts rather than wrong-password failures. The password was accepted and the sign-in was not completed at the next step.

skills.title: Password has expired
skills.description: Use when most failures carry the password-expired or must-change-password code in Active Directory or Entra ID. The password presented may be correct but is past its expiry and has to be changed.

skills.title: Not enough evidence to explain
skills.description: Use when there are no failures in the window, a log source the explanation would depend on is missing, signals conflict, or no other skill clearly fits. States what was checked and what is missing, and never guesses a cause.

skills.title: Clock on the source system is wrong
skills.description: Use when Kerberos failures carry the clock-skew code. The password is fine. The source system's clock differs too much from the domain's, so Kerberos rejects the request.

skills.title: Mail client or script sending a wrong password
skills.description: Use when Entra ID sign-in failures are bad-password errors coming from legacy clients such as Exchange ActiveSync, IMAP, POP, SMTP or other basic-authentication clients. Usually a phone, tablet or script holding an old password.

skills.title: Account was already locked or revoked
skills.description: Use when nearly all failures in the window carry the account-locked code or the ambiguous Kerberos revoked code. The window shows attempts bouncing off an account that was already locked, not the failures that caused the lockout.

skills.title: Account is not allowed to log on from there or then
skills.description: Use when most failures carry the workstation-restriction or logon-hours code. The password is correct but the account is restricted from logging on at that host or at that time.

skills.title: Old password still stored somewhere
skills.description: Use when failed logins for an account begin shortly after its password was changed or reset, and most failures are wrong-password errors from internal systems. Explains that something is still presenting the old password, and on which host.

skills.title: Failures from many or external sources
skills.description: Use when wrong-password or unknown-user failures arrive from external addresses, from many different sources in a short burst, or from many internet addresses against cloud sign-in. The pattern does not look like one misconfigured system and must go to the security operations team.

skills.title: Wrong password retries with no recent password change
skills.description: Use when an account shows wrong-password failures from internal systems and no password change or reset appears in the time window. Covers a stored password that went stale before the window began, and a person or script repeatedly presenting a wrong password.
